subject: chem
title: Coordination Compounds
syllabus: Introduction to coordination compounds. Werner's theory; ligands, coordination number, denticity, chelation; IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear co-ordination compounds, isomerism; Bonding — Valence bond approach and basic ideas of Crystal field theory, colour and magnetic properties; importance of co-ordination compounds (in qualitative analysis, extraction of metals and in biological systems).

body: [Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}: inside [ ] = coordination sphere (primary valence +3 shared with 2 free Cl^{−}); secondary valence = coordination number 6
Ionisable ions (outside [ ]) precipitate: free Cl^{−} → AgCl, free SO_{4}^{2−} → BaSO_{4}. Ions per formula decide conductivity and ΔT_{f} = iK_{f}m.
Denticity: en, C_{2}O_{4}^{2−} bidentate; EDTA^{4−} hexadentate. Ambidentate: NO_{2}^{−}/ONO^{−}, SCN^{−}/NCS^{−}. Homoleptic = one kind of ligand.

check.why: Only the Cl outside the bracket ionises.

body: Octahedral: t_{2g} (−0.4Δ_{o}) below e_{g} (+0.6Δ_{o}). Tetrahedral: e below t_{2}, Δ_{t} ≈ (4/9)Δ_{o}
Δ_{o} also grows with metal charge (M^{3+} > M^{2+}) and down a group (3d < 4d < 5d).
Colour: light of energy Δ is absorbed; we see the complementary colour. Bigger Δ → shorter λ absorbed.
d^{4}–d^{7} octahedral: Δ_{o} > P → low spin (fill t_{2g} first); Δ_{o} < P → high spin. μ = √(n(n + 2)) BM
Strong field: CN^{−}, CO, NO_{2}^{−} pair electrons. Co^{3+} (d^{6}) pairs even with NH_{3}, en, H_{2}O, C_{2}O_{4}^{2−}; [CoF_{6}]^{3−} stays high spin.
d^{1}–d^{3} and d^{8}–d^{10}: same configuration whatever the ligand. Tetrahedral complexes are always high spin; square planar d^{8} ([Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}) is diamagnetic.
CFSE = (−0.4x + 0.6y)Δ_{o} for t_{2g}^{x}e_{g}^{y}. High-spin d^{5} has CFSE 0.
CN 6: d^{2}sp^{3} (inner orbital, uses 3d) when two 3d orbitals are free — low spin or d^{0}–d^{3}; otherwise sp^{3}d^{2} (outer orbital, uses 4d).
CN 4: sp^{3} tetrahedral ([NiCl_{4}]^{2−}, [MnBr_{4}]^{2−}, Ni(CO)_{4}); dsp^{2} square planar ([Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}, Pt^{2+}).
Carbonyls: σ donation C → M plus π back-donation M(d) → CO π*. Synergic bonding strengthens M–C and weakens C≡O.
VBT gives no quantitative energies and cannot explain colour; CFT treats ligands as point charges.

check.why: Weak F⁻: high spin, outer 4d used.

body: Structural: ionisation, linkage, coordination, solvate. Stereo: geometrical (cis/trans, fac/mer) and optical
Octahedral counts: MA_{4}B_{2} 2; MA_{3}B_{3} 2 (fac, mer); M(AA)_{2}B_{2} 3 (trans + cis pair); M(AA)_{3} 2 (Δ, Λ); MA_{2}B_{2}C_{2} 6 (5 geometrical, one chiral).
Tetrahedral MABCD: no geometrical isomers, but chiral. Square planar MA_{2}B_{2}: cis/trans; MABCD: 3.
Chelate effect: en, oxalate and EDTA complexes are more stable than unidentate analogues.

traps: [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is low spin and diamagnetic (Co³⁺ has a large Δₒ).
Tetrahedral MABCD shows NO geometrical isomerism.
cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ gives 2 optical isomers; total stereoisomers 3.
Δₜ CFSE is in units of Δₜ, not Δₒ.
Synergic bonding STRENGTHENS the M–C bond.
Only ions OUTSIDE the square bracket react with AgNO₃.

steps.note: Coordination sphere, ligands, AgCl and conductivity
Low/high spin, CFSE and magnetic moments

pyq.q: Which of the following complex is homoleptic?
sol: Homoleptic = only one kind of ligand around the metal.
Only [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} has a single ligand type; the rest mix NH_{3} and Cl^{−}.

pyq.q: [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} and [CoF_{6}]^{3−} are respectively known as:
sol: Co^{3+} is d^{6}. NH_{3} pairs the electrons (t_{2g}^{6}, d^{2}sp^{3}, inner orbital) → spin paired.
F^{−} is weak field: t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}, 4 unpaired (sp^{3}d^{2}, outer orbital) → spin free.
o: Spin free Complex, Spin paired Complex
Spin paired Complex, Spin free Complex
Outer orbital Complex, Inner orbital Complex
Inner orbital Complex, Spin paired Complex

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): In octahedral complexes, when Δ_{o} < P high spin complexes are formed. When Δ_{o} > P low spin complexes are formed. Statement (II) : In tetrahedral complexes because of Δ_{t} < P, low spin complexes are rarely formed. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: I: the 4th electron goes to e_{g} (costs Δ_{o}) or pairs (costs P) — whichever is cheaper. True.
II: Δ_{t} = (4/9)Δ_{o} is small, almost always below P → tetrahedral complexes are high spin. True.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

pyq.q: A transition metal (M) among Mn, Cr, Co and Fe has the highest standard electrode potential (M^{3+}/M^{2+}). It forms a metal complex of the type [M(CN)_{6}]^{4−}. The number of electrons present in the e_{g} orbital of the complex is ______
sol: E°(M^{3+}/M^{2+}): Co +1.97 V is highest.
[Co(CN)_{6}]^{4−}: Co^{2+} d^{7}, CN^{−} strong field → t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1} → 1 electron in e_{g}.

pyq.q: Formation of Na_{4}[Fe(CN)_{5}NOS], a purple coloured complex formed by addition of sodium nitroprusside in sodium carbonate extract of salt indicates the presence of :
sol: S^{2−} adds to the NO of nitroprusside: [Fe(CN)_{5}NO]^{2−} + S^{2−} → [Fe(CN)_{5}NOS]^{4−} (purple).
So the test detects sulphide.

pyq.q: The d-orbital electronic configuration of the complex among [Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}, [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, [Mn(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} and [Zn(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} that has the highest CFSE is :
sol: Largest stabilisation: [Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}, t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}.

pyq.q: The spin-only magnetic moment value of M^{n+} ion formed among Ni, Zn, Mn and Cu that has the least enthalpy of atomisation is ______ . (in nearest integer) Here n is equal to the number of diamagnetic complexes among K_{2}[NiCl_{4}], [Zn(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{2}, K_{3}[Mn(CN)_{6}] and [Cu(PPh_{3})_{3}I]
sol: Least atomisation enthalpy: Zn (126 kJ/mol; no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding).

pyq.q: The correct order of the complexes [Co(NH_{3})_{5}(H_{2}O)]^{3+} (A), [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (B), [Co(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (C) and [CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+} (D) in terms of wavelength of light absorbed is
sol: Same Co^{3+}: Δ_{o} follows the ligand field — Cl^{−} < H_{2}O < NH_{3} < CN^{−}.
λ absorbed ∝ 1/Δ_{o}: D (one Cl^{−}) > A (one H_{2}O) > B (all NH_{3}) > C (CN^{−}).

pyq.q: The number of optical isomers exhibited by the iron complex (A) obtained from the following reaction is ______ FeCl_{3} + KOH + H_{2}C_{2}O_{4} → A
sol: Three chelate rings make a propeller with no mirror plane: Δ and Λ forms → 2 optical isomers.

pyq.q: Identify the diamagnetic octahedral complex ions from below ; A. [Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3−} B. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} C. [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{4−} D. [Co(H_{2}O)_{3}F_{3}]
sol: D: F^{−} keeps Co^{3+} high spin (t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}) → 4 unpaired. Diamagnetic: B and C.

pyq.q: Number of stereoisomers possible for the complexes, [CrCl_{3}(py)_{3}] and [CrCl_{2}(ox)_{2}]^{3−} are respectively (py = pyridine, ox = oxalate)
sol: [CrCl_{3}(py)_{3}] is MA_{3}B_{3}: fac and mer, both achiral → 2.
[CrCl_{2}(ox)_{2}]^{3−} is M(AA)_{2}B_{2}: trans (achiral) + cis (a pair of enantiomers) → 3.

pyq.q: Which one of the following complexes will have Δ_{0} = 0 and μ = 5.96 B.M.?
sol: μ = 5.96 BM ↔ 5 unpaired → high-spin d^{5}.
[FeF_{6}]^{4−} is d^{6} HS (4 unpaired); the other two are diamagnetic.

pyq.q: The correct order of [FeF_{6}]^{3−}, [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, [Ni(CO)_{4}] and [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} complex species based on the number of unpaired electrons present is :
sol: [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}: d^{8} square planar (dsp^{2}) → 0. [Ni(CO)_{4}]: Ni(0) 3d^{10} tetrahedral → 0.

pyq.q: A metal complex with a formula MCl_{4}·3NH_{3} is involved in sp^{3}d^{2} hybridisation. It upon reaction with excess of AgNO_{3} solution gives 'x' moles of AgCl. Consider 'x' is equal to the number of lone pairs of electron present in central atom of BrF_{5}. Then the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is ______.
sol: BrF_{5}: Br has 7 valence electrons, 5 used in bonds → 1 lone pair, so x = 1.
sp^{3}d^{2} → coordination number 6: one Cl^{−} is ionisable → [M(NH_{3})_{3}Cl_{3}]Cl.
MA_{3}B_{3} has fac and mer → 2 geometrical isomers.

pyq.q: If an iron (III) complex with the formula [Fe(NH_{3})_{x}(CN)_{y}]^{−} has no electron in its e_{g} orbital, then the value of x + y is
sol: No e_{g} electrons → octahedral low spin t_{2g}^{5}: six ligands, so x + y = 6.
Charge check: +3 − y = −1 → y = 4, x = 2.

pyq.q: The number of unpaired d-electrons in [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} is
sol: Co^{3+} is d^{6}. With its high charge, even H_{2}O gives Δ_{o} > P for Co^{3+}.
t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0} → 0 unpaired (diamagnetic, as NCERT treats it).

pyq.q: The correct sequence of ligands in the order of decreasing field strength is :
sol: Spectrochemical series (weak → strong): I^{−} < Br^{−} < S^{2−} < SCN^{−} < Cl^{−} < F^{−} < OH^{−} < C_{2}O_{4}^{2−} < H_{2}O < NCS^{−} < EDTA^{4−} < NH_{3} < en < CN^{−} < CO.
Only CO > H_{2}O > F^{−} > S^{2−} runs strictly downward.

pyq.q: Number of complexes from the following with even number of unpaired "d" electrons is [V(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}, [Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}, [Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}, [Ni(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}, [Cu(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} [Given atomic numbers : V = 23, Cr = 24, Fe = 26, Ni = 28, Cu = 29]
sol: Even: V^{3+} and Cr^{2+} → 2.

pyq.q: The metal atom present in the complex MABXL (where A, B, X and L are unidentate ligands and M is metal) involves sp^{3} hybridization. The number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is:
sol: sp^{3} → tetrahedral. Every pair of positions on a tetrahedron is equivalent (all at 109.5°), so there is no cis/trans distinction.
Geometrical isomers: 0 (MABXL is chiral, so it shows optical isomerism instead).

pyq.q: Which one of the following complexes will exhibit the least paramagnetic behaviour ? [Atomic number, Cr = 24, Mn = 25, Fe = 26, Co = 27 ]
sol: Fewest unpaired: [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}.

pyq.q: The correct order of ligands arranged in increasing field strength.
sol: Only Br^{−} < F^{−} < H_{2}O < NH_{3} rises throughout.

pyq.q: Match List-I (Tetrahedral Complex) with List-II (Electronic configuration): (A) TiCl_{4} (B) [FeO_{4}]^{2−} (C) [FeCl_{4}]^{−} (D) [CoCl_{4}]^{2−}; (I) e^{2}, t_{2}^{0} (II) e^{4}, t_{2}^{3} (III) e^{0}, t_{2}^{0} (IV) e^{2}, t_{2}^{3}
sol: Tetrahedral: lower e (2 orbitals), upper t_{2} (3 orbitals); always high spin.

pyq.q: Consider the following complexes. [CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+} (A), [Co(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (B), [Co(NH_{3})_{5}(H_{2}O)]^{3+} (C), [Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+} (D). The correct order of A, B, C and D in terms of wavenumber of light absorbed is :
sol: Wavenumber absorbed ∝ Δ.
D: Cu^{2+} (lower charge) with weak H_{2}O → smallest Δ. Among Co^{3+}: Cl^{−} (A) < H_{2}O (C) < CN^{−} (B).
D < A < C < B.

pyq.q: An octahedral complex having molecular composition Co·5NH_{3}·Cl·SO_{4} has two isomers A and B. The solution of A gives a white precipitate with AgNO_{3} solution and the solution of B gives white precipitate with BaCl_{2} solution. The type of isomerism exhibited by the complex is,
sol: Same formula, different ions released in solution → ionisation isomerism.

pyq.q: The number of paramagnetic complexes among [FeF_{6}]^{3−}, [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−}, [Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3−}, [Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−}, [MnCl_{6}]^{3−}, and [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, which involved d^{2}sp^{3} hybridization is
sol: d^{2}sp^{3} (inner orbital) needs the electrons pushed into t_{2g}: strong-field CN^{−}, and oxalate with Co^{3+}. F^{−}/Cl^{−} complexes are sp^{3}d^{2}.
Paramagnetic among them: 2.

pyq.q: The number of unpaired electrons responsible for the paramagnetic nature of the following complex species are respectively : [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−}, [FeF_{6}]^{3−}, [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, [Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3−}

The number of paramagnetic metal complex species among [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}, [Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−}, [MnCl_{6}]^{3−}, [Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3−}, [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−} and [FeF_{6}]^{3−} with same number of unpaired electrons is ______ .
sol: Paramagnetic ones sharing a count: [MnCl_{6}]^{3−} and [CoF_{6}]^{3−} (4 each) → 2.

pyq.q: Match List-I (Complex ion) with List-II (Spin only magnetic moment in B.M.): (A) [Cr(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (B) [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} (C) [CoF_{6}]^{3−} (D) [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}; (I) 4.90 (II) 3.87 (III) 0.0 (IV) 2.83
Total number of unpaired electrons in the complex ion [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} and [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} is

An octahedral complex with the formula CoCl_{3}nNH_{3} upon reaction with excess of AgNO_{3} solution given 2 moles of AgCl. Consider the oxidation state of Co in the complex is 'x'. The value of "x + n" is
sol: 2 AgCl → 2 ionisable Cl^{−}; the third Cl^{−} is coordinated. Octahedral → 5 NH_{3}: [Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}, n = 5.
Co is +3 → x + n = 8.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : N(CH_{3})_{3} and P(CH_{3})_{3} can act as ligands to form transition metal complexes. Statement II: As N and P are from same group, the nature of bonding of N(CH_{3})_{3} and P(CH_{3})_{3} is always same with transition metals. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: I: both have a lone pair to donate → both are ligands. True.
II: P has empty 3d (σ*) orbitals and accepts back-donation (σ-donor + π-acceptor); N cannot. False.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

pyq.q: Number of complexes with even number of electrons in t_{2g} orbitals is - [Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}, [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}, [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}, [Cu(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}, [Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}
sol: Even: 3.

pyq.q: The coordination environment of Ca^{2+} ion in its complex with EDTA^{4−} is :
sol: EDTA^{4−} is hexadentate (2 N + 4 O^{−} donors) and wraps one Ca^{2+}.
Six donor atoms → octahedral.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The total number of geometrical isomers shown by [Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{+} complex ion is three Reason (R): [Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{+} complex ion has an octahedral geometry. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: [Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{+} (octahedral, M(AA)_{2}B_{2}) has 2 geometrical isomers, cis and trans; only cis is chiral, giving 3 stereoisomers in all.
So (A) "three geometrical isomers" is wrong; (R) is right.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

pyq.q: Match List-I (Chromium (III) Complexes, en = ethylene diamine) with List-II (Δ_{0} in cm^{−1}): A. [Cr(CN)_{6}]^{3−} B. [CrF_{6}]^{3−} C. [Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} D. [Cr(en)_{3}]^{3+}; I. 15,060 II. 17,400 III. 22,300 IV. 26,600
sol: Same Cr^{3+}, so Δ_{o} follows the ligand: F^{−} < H_{2}O < en < CN^{−}.
Assign rising values: F^{−} 15,060; H_{2}O 17,400; en 22,300; CN^{−} 26,600 → A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

pyq.q: The correct increasing order of spin-only magnetic moment values of the complex ions [MnBr_{4}]^{2−} (A), [Cu(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} (B), [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} (C) and [Ni(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} (D) is :
sol: C < B < D < A.

pyq.q: The number of isoelectronic species among Sc^{3+}, Cr^{2+}, Mn^{3+}, Co^{3+} and Fe^{3+} is 'n'. If 'n' moles of AgCl is formed during the reaction of complex with formula CoCl_{3}(en)_{2}NH_{3} with excess of AgNO_{3} solution, then the number of electrons present in the t_{2g} orbital of the complex is ______ .
sol: Electrons: Sc^{3+} 18, Cr^{2+} 22, Mn^{3+} 22, Co^{3+} 24, Fe^{3+} 23 → Cr^{2+}, Mn^{3+} are isoelectronic, n = 2.
Two Cl^{−} are ionisable; (en)_{2} + NH_{3} + Cl fill 6 sites: [Co(en)_{2}(NH_{3})Cl]Cl_{2}.
Co^{3+} d^{6}, strong field → t_{2g}^{6}: 6 electrons.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Among Zn, Mn, Sc and Cu, the energy required to remove the third valence electron is highest for Zn and lowest for Sc. Statement II: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of CFSE is [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} < [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} < [Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: I: IE_{3} (kJ/mol) Sc 2393 (gives noble-gas Sc^{3+}), Mn 3260, Cu 3556, Zn 3837 (breaks d^{10}). True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism ? A. [Ag(NH_{3})_{2}][Ag(CN)_{2}] B. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}] C. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}] D. [Fe(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}] E. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Fe(CN)_{6}]
sol: Coordination isomerism: ligands swap between a cationic and an anionic complex of different metals, e.g. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}] ⇌ [Cr(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}].
A and C have the same metal on both sides — a swap gives back the same pair of metal centres. B, D, E qualify.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) of [Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+} is greater than that of [Mn(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}. Statement II: Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: II: K_{3}[Fe(CN)_{6}] (Fe^{3+} LS, 1 unpaired, 1.73 BM) vs Na_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}] (Fe^{2+} LS, 0). True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: In which of the following complexes the CFSE, Δ_{o} will be equal to zero ?
sol: CFSE = 0 needs high-spin d^{5} (or d^{0}/d^{10}).

pyq.q: Identify the homoleptic complex(es) that is/are low spin. (A) [Fe(CN)_{5}NO]^{2−} (B) [CoF_{6}]^{3−} (C) [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{4−} (D) [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (E) [Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}
sol: (A) has CN^{−} and NO → heteroleptic, out.

pyq.q: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of their crystal field stabilization energies is :
sol: Tetrahedral Δ_{t} = (4/9)Δ_{o} → the 4-coordinate Co^{2+} complex is lowest (−1.2Δ_{t} ≈ −0.53Δ_{o}).

pyq.q: The complex of Ni^{2+} ion and dimethyl glyoxime contains ______ number of Hydrogen (H) atoms.
sol: Dimethylglyoxime is C_{4}H_{8}N_{2}O_{2}; each binds as dmgH^{−} after losing one O–H proton.
[Ni(dmgH)_{2}]: 2 × 7 = 14 H (two of them in the O–H···O bridges).

pyq.q: The complex that shows Facial - Meridional isomerism is:
sol: fac/mer needs MA_{3}B_{3}: three of one ligand on a face (fac) or along a meridian (mer).
[Co(NH_{3})_{3}Cl_{3}] is MA_{3}B_{3}; the others are MA_{4}B_{2} (cis/trans), M(AA)_{2}B_{2} (cis/trans) and M(AA)_{3}.

pyq.q: The d-electronic configuration of an octahedral Co (II) complex having magnetic moment of 3.95 BM is:
sol: 3.95 BM ≈ √15 → 3 unpaired electrons.
Co^{2+} d^{7} octahedral: low spin t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1} has 1; high spin t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2} has 3 → t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2}.

pyq.q: CrCl_{3}·xNH_{3} can exist as a complex. 0.1 molal aqueous solution of this complex shows a depression in freezing point of 0.558°C. Assuming 100% ionisation of this complex and coordination number of Cr is 6, the complex will be (Given K_{f} = 1.86 K kg mol^{−1})
sol: i = ΔT_{f}/(K_{f}m) = 0.558/(1.86 × 0.1) = 3 ions per formula unit.

pyq.q: Identify the coordination complexes in which the central metal ion has d^{4} configuration. (A) [FeO_{4}]^{2−} (B) [Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (C) [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (D) Cr_{2}(O–CO–Me)_{4}(H_{2}O)_{2} (E) [NiF_{6}]^{2−}
sol: Oxidation states: Fe^{+6} (d^{2}), Mn^{+3} (d^{4}), Fe^{+3} (d^{5}), Cr^{+2} in chromium(II) acetate (d^{4}), Ni^{+4} (d^{6}).
d^{4}: B and D.

pyq.q: One mole of the octahedral complex compound Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl_{3} gives 3 moles of ions on dissolution in water. One mole of the same complex reacts with excess of AgNO_{3} solution to yield two moles of AgCl_{(s)}. The structure of the complex is:
sol: 2 AgCl → 2 free Cl^{−}; 3 ions = 1 complex cation + 2 Cl^{−}.
Octahedral: 5 NH_{3} + 1 Cl inside → [Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}.

pyq.q: The conditions and consequence that favours the t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1} configuration in a metal complex are :
sol: d^{4}: the 4th electron enters e_{g} only if Δ_{o} < P — a weak field ligand.
With 4 unpaired electrons it is a high spin complex.
o: strong field ligand, low spin complex
strong field ligand, high spin complex
weak field ligand, high spin complex
weak field ligand, low spin complex

pyq.q: Consider the following complex ions P = [FeF_{6}]^{3−}, Q = [V(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}, R = [Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{2+}. The correct order of the complex ions, according to their spin only magnetic moment values (in B.M.) is:
sol: Q < R < P.

pyq.q: The Spin only magnetic moment value of square planar complex [Pt(NH_{3})_{2}Cl(NH_{2}CH_{3})]Cl is ______ B.M. (Nearest integer) (Given atomic number for Pt = 78 )
sol: Square planar (dsp^{2}) d^{8}: the high-energy d_{x²−y²} stays empty, all 8 electrons pair → 0 BM.

pyq.q: The metal ion whose electronic configuration is not affected by the nature of the ligand and which gives a violet colour in non-luminous flame under hot condition in borax bead test is
sol: Octahedral d^{1}–d^{3} and d^{8}–d^{10} have the same t_{2g}/e_{g} filling in weak and strong fields; d^{4}–d^{7} depend on the ligand. So Mn^{2+} (d^{5}) is out.
Borax bead (hot, oxidising flame): Ni — violet; Cr — green; Ti — colourless. → Ni^{2+} (d^{8}: t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2} always).

pyq.q: Match List - I (Complex) with List - II (Hybridisation of central metal ion): (A) [CoF_{6}]^{3−} (B) [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} (C) [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (D) [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}; (I) d^{2}sp^{3} (II) sp^{3} (III) sp^{3}d^{2} (IV) dsp^{2}
sol: [CoF_{6}]^{3−}: weak F^{−}, outer 4d used → sp^{3}d^{2}. [NiCl_{4}]^{2−}: tetrahedral sp^{3}.
[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}: electrons paired, two 3d free → d^{2}sp^{3}. [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−}: square planar dsp^{2}.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Complex) with List - II (Hybridisation & Magnetic characters): (A) [MnBr_{4}]^{2−} (B) [FeF_{6}]^{3−} (C) [Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−} (D) [Ni(CO)_{4}]; (I) d^{2}sp^{3} & diamagnetic (II) sp^{3}d^{2} & paramagnetic (III) sp^{3} & diamagnetic (IV) sp^{3} & paramagnetic
sol: [MnBr_{4}]^{2−}: tetrahedral sp^{3}, Mn^{2+} d^{5} → paramagnetic. [FeF_{6}]^{3−}: sp^{3}d^{2}, 5 unpaired.
[Co(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−}: Co^{3+} d^{6} paired → d^{2}sp^{3}, diamagnetic. [Ni(CO)_{4}]: Ni(0) 3d^{10}, sp^{3}, diamagnetic.

pyq.q: Identify the homoleptic complexes with odd number of d electrons in the central metal : (A) [FeO_{4}]^{2−} (B) [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (C) [Fe(CN)_{5}NO]^{2−} (D) [CoCl_{4}]^{2−} (E) [Co(H_{2}O)_{3}F_{3}]
sol: Homoleptic: A (only O^{2−}), B (only CN^{−}), D (only Cl^{−}); C and E mix ligands.

pyq.q: Consider the following low-spin complexes K_{3}[Co(NO_{2})_{6}], K_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}], K_{3}[Fe(CN)_{6}], Cu_{2}[Fe(CN)_{6}] and Zn_{2}[Fe(CN)_{6}]. The sum of the spin-only magnetic moment values of complexes having yellow colour is ______ B.M. (answer in nearest integer)
sol: Yellow: K_{3}[Co(NO_{2})_{6}] and K_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}]. (K_{3}[Fe(CN)_{6}] is red, Cu_{2}[Fe(CN)_{6}] chocolate-brown, Zn_{2}[Fe(CN)_{6}] white.)
Both are low-spin d^{6} (Co^{3+}, Fe^{2+}) → 0 + 0 = 0 BM.

pyq.q: Consider the transition metal ions Mn^{3+}, Cr^{3+}, Fe^{3+} and Co^{3+} and all form low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals of the complexes is

Choose the correct Statements from the following: (A) Ethane-1, 2-diamine is a chelating ligand. (B) Metallic aluminium is produced by electrolysis of aluminium oxide in presence of cryolite. (C) Cyanide ion is used as ligand for leaching of silver. (D) Phosphine act as a ligand in Wilkinson catalyst. (E) The stability constants of Ca^{2+} and Mg^{2+} are similar with EDTA complexes.
sol: A: en binds through both N → chelate. B: Hall–Héroult electrolysis of Al_{2}O_{3} in molten cryolite. C: Ag forms [Ag(CN)_{2}]^{−} in cyanide leaching. D: Wilkinson catalyst is [RhCl(PPh_{3})_{3}]. All true.
E is false: Ca^{2+}–EDTA is far more stable than Mg^{2+}–EDTA (which is why the two can be titrated separately).
The only option with no false statement is (A), (B), (C).

pyq.q: Number of complexes which show optical isomerism among the following is ______. cis−[Cr(ox)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{3−}, [Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}, cis−[Pt(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{2+}, cis−[Co(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{+}, trans−[Pt(en)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{2+}, trans−[Cr(ox)_{2}Cl_{2}]^{3−}
sol: cis-M(AA)_{2}B_{2} has no mirror plane → optically active; trans-M(AA)_{2}B_{2} has one → inactive.
M(AA)_{3} ([Co(en)_{3}]^{3+}) is chiral.
Active: the three cis complexes + [Co(en)_{3}]^{3+} = 4.

pyq.q: The correct statements from following are: A. The strength of anionic ligands can be explained by crystal field theory. B. Valence bond theory does not give a quantitative interpretation of kinetic stability of coordination compounds. C. The hybridization involved in formation of [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} complex is dsp^{2}. D. The number of possible isomer(s) of cis-[PtCl_{2}(en)_{2}]^{2+} is one
sol: A false: CFT treats ligands as point charges, so anions should split most — yet halides sit at the weak end. CFT cannot explain this.
B true: VBT gives no quantitative account of stability. C true: square planar dsp^{2}.
D false: cis-[PtCl_{2}(en)_{2}]^{2+} is chiral → a pair of enantiomers (2).

pyq.q: Consider the metal complexes [Ni(en)_{3}]^{2+} (A), [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} (B) and [Ni(NH_{3})_{6}]^{2+} (C). Choose the CORRECT option by considering the number of unpaired electrons present in (A), (B) and (C) respectively and the order of frequency of absorption.
sol: Ni^{2+} d^{8}: octahedral t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2} → 2 unpaired whatever the ligand; tetrahedral [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} → 2 as well.
Absorbed frequency ∝ Δ: en > NH_{3} (octahedral), and tetrahedral Cl^{−} has the smallest Δ (Δ_{t} ≈ 4/9 Δ_{o}, weak ligand) → A > C > B.

pyq.q: [Ni(PPh_{3})_{2}Cl_{2}] is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex. A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism. B. The complex is white in colour. C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is 2.84 BM. D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of Ni in this complex is −0.8Δ_{o}. E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in Ni(CO)_{4}.
sol: Paramagnetic Ni^{2+} d^{8} with 4 ligands → tetrahedral (sp^{3}), like Ni(CO)_{4} — E correct.
A wrong: tetrahedral MA_{2}B_{2} has no geometrical isomers. B wrong: d–d transitions make it coloured.
C correct: 2 unpaired → √8 = 2.83 BM. D wrong: e^{4}t_{2}^{4} gives −0.8Δ_{t} (≈ −0.36Δ_{o}), not −0.8Δ_{o}.
Incorrect: A, B, D.

pyq.q: The correct statements about metal carbonyls are A. The metal-carbon bonds in metal carbonyls possess both σ and π character. B. Due to synergic bonding interactions between metal and CO ligand, the metal-carbon bond becomes weak. C. The metal-carbon σ bond is formed by the donation of lone pair of electrons on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant orbital of metal. D. The metal-carbon π bond is formed by the donation of electrons from filled d-orbital of metal into vacant π* orbital of CO.
sol: σ: C lone pair → empty metal orbital (C). π: filled metal d → CO π* (D). So M–C has both characters (A).
Synergic bonding strengthens the M–C bond (and weakens C≡O) — B is false.

pyq.q: The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are : A. It is red in colour. B. It has a high solubility in water at pH = 9. C. The Ni ion has two unpaired d-electrons. D. The N–Ni–N bond angle is almost close to 90°. E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles (metal containing rings).
sol: [Ni(dmgH)_{2}] is a red, water-insoluble precipitate (that is how Ni^{2+} is detected) — A correct, B incorrect.
Square planar d^{8} → no unpaired electrons — C incorrect. Square planar → N–Ni–N ≈ 90° — D correct.
It has two five-membered Ni–N–C–C–N chelate rings plus two six-membered H-bonded rings, not four five-membered ones — E incorrect.

pyq.q: The crystal field splitting energy of [Co(oxalate)_{3}]^{3−} complex is 'n' times that of the [Cr(oxalate)_{3}]^{3−} complex. Here 'n' is ______. (Assume Δ_{o} >> P)
sol: With Δ_{o} ≫ P both are low spin. Co^{3+} d^{6} t_{2g}^{6}: CFSE = −2.4Δ_{o}. Cr^{3+} d^{3} t_{2g}^{3}: −1.2Δ_{o}.
Same ligand, same Δ_{o} assumed → n = 2.4/1.2 = 2.

pyq.q: Identify the correct statements from the following A. [Fe(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−} is the most stable complex among [Fe(OH)_{6}]^{3−}, [Fe(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}]^{3−} and [Fe(SCN)_{6}]^{3−} B. The stability of [Cu(NH_{3})_{4}]^{2+} is greater than that of [Cu(en)_{2}]^{2+} C. The hybridization of Fe in K_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}] is d^{2}sp^{3} D. [Fe(NO_{2})_{3}Cl_{3}]^{3−} exhibits linkage isomerism E. NO_{2}^{−} and SCN^{−} ligands are NOT ambidentate ligands
sol: A: oxalate is the only chelating ligand there → chelate effect → most stable. True.
B: two chelating en beat four NH_{3} (chelate effect) — false. C: Fe^{2+} d^{6} LS → d^{2}sp^{3}. True.
D: NO_{2}^{−} binds via N (nitro) or O (nitrito) → linkage isomers. True. E: NO_{2}^{−} and SCN^{−} are ambidentate — false.
o: A, B, C, D and E

pyq.q: The total number of unpaired electrons present in the d^{3}, d^{4} (low spin) d^{5} (high spin), d^{6} (high spin) and d^{7} (low spin) octahedral complex systems is ______ .

Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following: A. [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} : Inner orbital complex; d^{2}sp^{3} hybridized B. [MnCl_{6}]^{3−} : Outer orbital complex; sp^{3}d^{2} hybridized C. [CoF_{6}]^{3−} : Outer orbital complex; d^{2}sp^{3} hybridized D. [FeF_{6}]^{3−} : Outer orbital complex; sp^{3}d^{2} hybridized E. [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} : Inner orbital complex; sp^{3} hybridized
sol: Inner orbital (n−1)d used when electrons pair: [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} d^{2}sp^{3} ✓.
[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} is dsp^{2} (square planar), not sp^{3} ✗. → A, B, D.

pyq.q: Which of the following are true about the energy of the given d-orbitals of a tetrahedral complex? A. d_{xy} = d_{xz} > d_{x²−y²} B. d_{xy} = d_{yz} > d_{z²} C. d_{x²−y²} > d_{z²} > d_{xz} D. d_{x²−y²} = d_{z²} < d_{xz}
sol: Tetrahedral splitting is inverted: t_{2} (d_{xy}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}) lies above e (d_{x²−y²}, d_{z²}); orbitals within a set are degenerate.
A, B, D fit; C wrongly splits the e pair and puts d_{xz} lowest.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The number of paramagnetic species among [CoF_{6}]^{3−}, [TiF_{6}]^{3−}, V_{2}O_{5} and [Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3−} is 3. Statement II: K_{4}[Fe(CN)_{6}] < K_{3}[Fe(CN)_{6}] < [Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]SO_{4}·H_{2}O < [Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{3} is the correct order in terms of number of unpaired electron(s) present in the complexes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Which of the following sequences of hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature are correct for the given coordination compounds ? A. [NiCl_{4}]^{2−} − sp^{3}, tetrahedral, paramagnetic B. [Ni(NH_{3})_{6}]^{2+} − sp^{3}d^{2}, octahedral, paramagnetic C. [Ni(CO)_{4}] − sp^{3}, tetrahedral, paramagnetic D. [Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2−} − dsp^{2}, square planar, diamagnetic
sol: A: Ni^{2+} d^{8} tetrahedral → 2 unpaired ✓. B: d^{8} octahedral can only use outer 4d (sp^{3}d^{2}), 2 unpaired ✓.
C: Ni(0) 3d^{10} → diamagnetic ✗. D: dsp^{2}, all paired ✓. → A, B, D.

pyq.q: Treatment of a gas 'X' with a freshly prepared ferrous sulphate solution gives a compound 'Y' as a brown ring. The compounds X and Y are.
sol: Nitrate is reduced by Fe^{2+} (conc. H_{2}SO_{4}) to NO; NO then binds Fe^{2+}.
Brown ring: [Fe(H_{2}O)_{5}(NO)]^{2+}, written here as [Fe(NO)]SO_{4}.

pyq.q: The wavelength of light absorbed for the following complexes are in the order [Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+} (I); [Co(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} (II); [Co(CN)_{6}]^{3−} (III); [Co(NH_{3})_{5}(H_{2}O)]^{3+} (IV); [CoF_{6}]^{3−} (V)
sol: Shortest λ for CN^{−}, then all-NH_{3}, then 5 NH_{3}+H_{2}O, then H_{2}O, then F^{−}: III < I < IV < II < V.

pyq.q: A chromium complex with a formula CrCl_{3}·6H_{2}O has a spin only magnetic moment value of 3.87 BM and its solution conductivity corresponds to 1: 2 electrolyte. 2.75 g of the complex solution was initially passed through a cation exchanger. The solution obtained after the process was reacted with excess of AgNO_{3}. The amount of AgCl formed in the above process is ______ g. (Nearest integer) [Given: Molar mass in g mol^{−1} Cr : 52; Cl : 35.5, Ag : 108, O : 16, H : 1]
sol: 1 : 2 electrolyte → [Cr(H_{2}O)_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}·H_{2}O (3.87 BM = Cr^{3+} d^{3}). The cation exchanger keeps the complex cation and releases 2H^{+}; the 2 free Cl^{−} pass through.
